chunks: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad b. Ibrahim al-Talaqani, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad b. al-Qasim al-Anbari narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad b. Abi Ya'qub al-Dinawari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi al-Miqdam al-'Ijli narrated to us. He said: It is narrated that

A man came to Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have a need from you.' He said: 'Write it on the ground, for I can see hardship plainly upon you.' So the man wrote on the ground: 'I am poor and in need.' Ali, peace be upon him, said: 'O Qanbar, clothe him in two garments.' The man then stood up and recited poetry, saying: 'You have clothed me in a suit whose beauties will wear out, but I shall clothe you in garments of beautiful praise.

If you have gained my good praise, you have gained a noble thing, and you will not find what you have gained wanting as a substitute. Indeed, praise keeps alive the memory of its bearer, like rain that brings life to the plains and the mountains. Never grow weary of a kindness you have begun, for every servant shall be recompensed according to what he did.'

Ali, peace be upon him, said: 'Give him one hundred dinars.' It was said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, you have already made him wealthy!' He said: 'I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, say: Put people in their proper stations.' Then Ali, peace be upon him, said: 'Indeed, I am astonished at peoples who buy slaves with their wealth but do not buy the loyalty of free people with their good deeds.'

key_terms.أَنْزِلُوا النَّاسَ مَنَازِلَهُمْ: Put people in their proper stations — a Prophetic teaching to treat people according to their dignity and worth
key_terms.الْأَحْرَار: Free people — contrasted with slaves to highlight that kindness can earn loyalty more valuable than ownership
key_terms.الْمَمَالِيك: Slaves/bondspeople — used here in contrast with free people to make a moral point about generosity
key_terms.حُلَّة: Hulla — a suit of two garments, a traditional Arabic gift of honor
key_terms.مَعْرُوف: Ma'ruf — kindness, good deeds, acts of benevolence

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali treat a poor man who came to him for help, and what Prophetic teaching did he cite?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Amali al-Saduq recounts an episode during Imam Ali's caliphate in Kufa, where a man came to him seeking help but was too ashamed to state his need aloud. Ali, perceiving his distress, asked him to write his request on the ground to spare his dignity. When the man wrote that he was poor and in need, Ali immediately ordered his servant Qanbar to clothe him in two garments. The man then recited eloquent poetry expressing his gratitude, likening good praise to rain that brings life to plains and mountains. Ali, moved by the man's eloquence and dignity, awarded him one hundred dinars. When questioned about the generosity, Ali cited the Prophet Muhammad's teaching: 'Put people in their proper stations.' He then reflected on the irony that some people spend their wealth buying slaves but neglect to earn the loyalty of free people through acts of kindness.
